profiled_workloads.selection_reason: Lowest-speedup workload of the round (0.925x); chosen first to test whether the small-shape loss is kernel geometry or fixed per-call overhead. Shape 1x8x7168 -> 1x7168.

Second small-shape workload (shape 2x8x7168 -> 2x7168) and the highest eval latency of the round; profiled to verify that the small-shape regime is a shared per-call floor rather than a per-shape kernel effect.
Third small-shape workload (shape 8x8x7168 -> 8x7168); completes the floor-regime sample and shows the non-monotonic eval latency that bounds the noise band of the small shapes.

Regime boundary: speedup jumps from ~1.0 to 2.47 here and this is the highest eval latency among the mid shapes, so it separates the L2-resident regime from the HBM-streaming regime. Shape 512x8x7168 -> 512x7168.

Highest-latency workload (0.487 ms, 87% of the round's total measured device time) and the only one whose eval latency is device-bound; it carries the frozen hypothesis's predicted 4096-token win. Shape 4096x8x7168 -> 4096x7168.

findings.label: Small-shape eval latency is a shared per-call floor: the device kernel is only 2-9% of measured latency for 1/2/8-token shapes
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary Task Duration / Task Wait Time, 10 warmup + 100 measured invocations per workload

evidence.metric: min_duration_us (best-case device time of the kernel on the 1-token shape) against authoritative eval latency 91.48 us
Task Wait Time per launch (host-side queueing, 100 launches)

findings.inference: For the three smallest shapes the measured device work (1.79/4.03/7.59 us) is 2-9% of the authoritative eval latency (91.5/93.8/85.0 us), and the profiled launches show ~45-830 us of host-side wait between back-to-back launches. The remaining ~85-90 us per call is a fixed dispatch/measurement floor that the reference implementation pays too (reference 84.7/92.8/85.7 us), so tile geometry, program count or masking cannot move these workloads. The three latencies are also non-monotonic in token count (1 token slower than 8 tokens), so the 0.925-1.009 speedups sit inside roughly +-7% floor noise and should not be optimized against directly.

findings.label: Load (MTE2) and vector pipes are ~89% serialized on every shape: pipe busy ratios sum to ~1.11 instead of ~1.0
findings.backend_detail: msprof AIV pipe counters; aiv_*_time values are per-core averages and the ratios are fractions of aiv_time, so ratios summing above 1.0 indicate concurrent-but-limited pipe occupancy

evidence.metric: aiv pipe busy ratios (vec+mte2+scalar+mte3) vs aiv_time
aiv pipe busy ratios (vec+mte2+scalar+mte3) vs aiv_time
aiv pipe busy ratios (vec+mte2+scalar+mte3) vs aiv_time
aiv_vec_time_us / aiv_mte2_time_us on the largest shape

findings.inference: On all five workloads the per-pipe busy times nearly add up to aiv_time (vec+mte2+scalar+mte3 = 1.11-1.12x aiv_time, i.e. only ~11% overlap), which is the signature of a load-convert-accumulate chain that executes its eight top_k loads and its vector reduce mostly in sequence rather than in a double-buffered pipeline. The frozen hypothesis predicted num_stages=2 would hide the eight strided top_k loads; the counters do not support that. The loads are still much faster than round 1 because of the BM=16 geometry, not because of overlap. Plumbing implication: if MTE2 were fully hidden under the vector reduce, the 4096-token kernel would approach its 323.9 us MTE2 time rather than 482.4-485.5 us.

findings.label: 4096-token shape is device-bound at ~1.09 TB/s effective GM traffic, with MTE2 (GM->L1) at 67% of AIV time
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary on 10 warmup + 100 measured invocations; launches are back-to-back with Task Wait Time ~0 us, so the device is saturated and host is not a factor here

evidence.metric: kernel duration vs authoritative eval latency (485.50 us vs 487.31 us = 99.6% device)
aiv_mte2_ratio (GM->L1 load pipe share of AIV time)
effective GM bandwidth derived from Input Shapes 4096,8,7168 bf16 + Output 4096,7168 bf16 (528.5 MB) over 485.5 us

findings.inference: This shape is the only one where eval latency equals device time, so it is the only workload whose speedup (4.95x) is a pure kernel quality signal. Reading 469.8 MB and writing 58.7 MB in 485.5 us is ~1.09 TB/s effective; the read pipe alone sustains ~1.45 TB/s over its 323.9 us of activity. Combined with the ~11% overlap finding, the gap between 485.5 us and the ~324-340 us implied by MTE2 alone suggests the remaining loss is overlap rather than raw HBM throughput - but this cannot be separated from an HBM ceiling with counters alone, because the bytes are irreducible (all eight top_k slices must be read).

findings.label: 512-token shape's 58.7 MB input fits the 176 MB L2, dropping MTE2 to 31% and making the shape vector-bound
findings.backend_detail: msprof AIV pipe counters; L2 attribution is inferred from the target's declared 176160768-byte L2 size

evidence.metric: kernel duration vs authoritative eval latency (36.40 us vs 102.38 us = 35.5% device)
effective GM bandwidth implied by 58.7 MB read + 7.34 MB write over 36.4 us

findings.inference: The 512-token workload moves the same per-block work as the 4096-token one (same BM=16/BN=1024 tile, 224 blocks) yet its MTE2 time is 29x lower (10.96 us vs 323.92 us) while its vector time scales linearly (24.62 us vs 184.93 us, 8x for 8x tokens). An implied 1.82 TB/s exceeds any plausible HBM rate on this part, so the reads are being served from the 176 MB L2 (input 58.7 MB fits; the 4096-token input at 469.8 MB does not). Consequently this shape is vector-bound on the device and, at 36.4 us kernel against 102.4 us eval latency, is still ~65 us floor-bound, so its 2.47x speedup mixes both regimes.

performance_interpretation: Round 2 is a large, real win: geo_mean 1.0117 -> 1.6234 (+60.5%), driven by the 4096-token shape falling 1.437 ms -> 0.487 ms (1.67x -> 4.95x) and the 512-token shape 0.153 ms -> 0.102 ms (1.62x -> 2.47x). The profiler confirms the geometry half of the frozen hypothesis (BM=16 packs 16 tokens per program, grid 1792 blocks, effective traffic ~1.09 TB/s versus round 1's ~0.38 TB/s) but contradicts the pipelining half: on every shape the AIV pipe busy ratios sum to ~1.11 rather than ~1.0, so MTE2 loads run ~89% serially with the vector reduce and num_stages=2 is not hiding their latency. Four of five workloads also remain dominated by something other than the kernel: three small shapes have 1.8-7.6 us kernels inside an ~85-94 us per-call floor shared with the reference, and the 512-token shape has a 36.4 us kernel inside a 102.4 us measurement. Therefore the only workload with kernel-side headroom is the 4096-token shape, where ~150 us of its 485.5 us is non-overlapped load time. The round's remaining lever is overlap, not more geometry.

next_experiment.action_description: On the mask-free contiguous kernel only, make the top_k accumulation pipelinable and deepen the load pipeline: replace the fully unrolled `for topk_index in tl.static_range(0, K)` load-and-accumulate body with a pipelinable loop form (a constexpr-bound `tl.range(0, K)` loop, keeping `reduced += tl.load(...).to(tl.float32)`) and run it at num_stages=3 with the existing BM=16 / BN=1024 tile and num_warps=4. If staging is rejected by the compiler or exceeds the UB budget (64 KB fp32 accumulator + 3 x 32 KB bf16 stage buffers), keep the same loop form and fall back to BN=512 with num_stages=4; do not change BM, the grid, the launcher's constexpr plumbing, or the strided fallback kernel in the same round.
next_experiment.expected_impact: If the ~89% serialization is pipeline construction rather than an HBM ceiling, the 4096-token kernel should approach its measured 323.9 us MTE2 time (485.5 -> ~350-400 us, speedup 4.95x -> 6.0-6.9x) and the 512-token kernel should approach its vector time (36.4 -> ~25-30 us, speedup 2.47x -> ~2.7-3.0x), lifting geo_mean from 1.6234 to roughly 1.68-1.75. The three small shapes should not move at all, because they sit at the shared per-call floor.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: Risks: (1) a depth-3 stage buffer may exceed the 192 KB UB and either fail to compile or spill, which would slow the kernel instead of speeding it up; (2) the Triton-Ascend compiler may re-unroll a constexpr-bound loop, in which case the counter signature does not change and the round is wasted but not harmful; (3) deeper staging can raise per-block register/UB pressure and shrink occupancy on the mid shape. Rollback: revert to the round-2 candidate exactly (BM=16, BN=1024, static_range over K, num_stages=2, num_warps=4) if the full-eval geo_mean falls below 1.6234, if any correctness workload stops reporting abs_err=0 / rel_err=0 / matched_ratio=1, or if the 512-token workload regresses above 0.102 ms.
success_criteria: Full eval correctness PASSES: all three correctness workloads keep abs_err=0, rel_err=0 and matched_ratio=1.
Headline geo_mean >= 1.70 (strictly better than round 2's 1.6234) with no workload regressing.
4096-token workload (00004) eval latency <= 0.44 ms, i.e. speedup >= 5.5x versus 4.95x now - the direct test of the overlap hypothesis.
512-token workload (00003) eval latency <= 0.095 ms (speedup >= 2.6x) and its kernel stays below 36.4 us.
The three small shapes (00000/00001/00002) stay within the observed floor noise, speedup >= 0.90; they are not expected to improve.

Falsification: if 00004's aiv_mte2_ratio is still >= 0.60 and its kernel duration stays near 485 us with pipe ratios still summing to ~1.11, overlap is not achievable at the Triton level for this tile and the next lever should be an instruction-level look (instruction_listing) or a manual double-buffered tile rather than further num_stages tuning.

warnings: msprof timing is diagnostic and is not eval latency; all speedup, latency and delta numbers in this analysis come from get_profile_context.

The three small-shape speedups (0.925 / 0.990 / 1.009) are inside the +-7% per-call floor noise: eval latency is non-monotonic in token count (91.5 us at 1 token, 85.0 us at 8 tokens) while the kernel is 1.8-7.6 us.
Only 'metrics' and 'instruction' profile levels are advertised on this backend; there is no 'source' level, so no source-line hotspot localization was attempted beyond kernel entry locators.
aiv_*_time counters are per-core averages and aiv_*_ratio values are fractions of aiv_time, not wall-clock; ratios summing above 1.0 mean concurrent pipe occupancy of ~11%, not 111% utilization.

The profile-level summary for 00000 reports avg_time_us 1.79 while the op_summary CSV contains the 100 per-invocation rows (the first few warm-up-adjacent rows are 4.2-4.9 us and are included in that average).
open_questions: Can the ~150 us of non-overlapped MTE2 time on the 4096-token shape actually be hidden at this tile size, or is BN=1024/BM=16 already limited by the per-core MTE2 issue rate rather than by staging depth?

Is aiv_mte2_time on this backend a per-core busy time or a bus-level occupancy counter? The 1.45 TB/s read-only figure computed from it is high enough that this matters for judging how close the shape is to the HBM ceiling.

What exactly constitutes the ~85 us per-call floor that both the candidate and the reference pay, and is any part of it attributable to the candidate's launcher (torch.empty, block-size while-loops, is_contiguous, 8-kwarg Triton launch) rather than to the harness?
Would an instruction-level listing show the eight top_k loads issued as separate bulk MTE2 ops each followed by a vector sync, which would confirm the serialization mechanism directly?
Whether the 512-token workload's L2-resident behaviour can be exploited deliberately (e.g. a smaller working set per program) for mid-size shapes.
